title: Dave Frank and the 12th Street Rag
summary: Dave Frank's son, the writer of 12th Street Rag, and how recordings differ from sheet music.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Oh, yeah. Do you remember a song plug I thought of? Dave Frank. He used to run the music department at Whirlines in late years.
I knew him. I don't remember that I knew him as a song plugger.
Well, his son told me about it. And so I sent him a list of questions. Like he actually knew the man who wrote 12th Street Rag.
Oh, uh-huh. And, uh... I used to play that, too. Yeah.
The man, uh... I think he ended up in Fort Worth, Texas or someplace like that.
He made a recording of it. It's different. The recording is different from the way it's written down, you know.

Mm-hmm. Well, now, for instance, as I said, that Alabama Bound, it's been so long since I've sat down and even looked at the music or anything that it may have appeared to be a little different in spots. I don't know.
But, uh... Uh... Anyway, there it is, and here I am.
